en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Cittāgāra-vagga 42.
The Training Rule on Using High Beds.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were using high chairs and couches.
People, while wandering on a tour of the monastery, saw this and complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can these bhikkhunīs use high chairs and couches? They are just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures!"
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can these bhikkhunīs use high seats and luxurious couches?"... [as before]...
“Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunīs use high seats and luxurious couches?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunīs use high seats and luxurious couches?
This, monks, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule: [The training rule follows.]
“Whichever bhikkhunī, however, should use a high couch or a luxurious couch, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
“Whichever, however,” means whichever such [person]... [and so forth].
"Bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the type of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Āsandī" (a high couch) means:
It is called "exceeding the proper measure.
A *pallaṅka* is said to be one made of imported animal skins.
"Should enjoy" means:
if he sits down on it or lies down on it, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense—
If she cuts off the legs of a chair and uses it,
or breaks the wickerwork of a couch and uses it,
[there is an offense] for one who is insane.
"Regarding the first offender":
thus ends the second training rule.
